author: DTrim99
body:
The title says PA, but the input row (`state=20`) and the attached return are both Maine, so I've treated it as Maine.

The standard-deduction gap comes from the **pension income deduction** (Schedule 1S, line 4). PolicyEngine deducts $45,864 of the $120,905 pension, giving Maine AGI of $222,669.44. The page-4 phaseout then leaves a standard deduction of $6,926.35. TaxAct deducts $0, giving Maine AGI of $268,533, so the standard deduction phases out fully. Both apply the phaseout the same way; they start from different Maine AGI.

On age: Maine has no general age-55 test. The [2024 Schedule 1S instructions (p. 2)](https://www.maine.gov/revenue/sites/maine.gov.revenue/files/inline-files/24_Form%201040ME_Sch%201S_ff.pdf#page=2) apply age 55 only to 457(b) plans:
> "…pension income from 457(b) plans received prior to age 55 that is not part of a series of equal periodic payments … may not be included in the deductible pension amount."

and exclude:
> "…distributions subject to the additional 10% federal tax on early distributions."

> "*Eligible pension income does not include benefits earned by another person, except in the case of a surviving spouse."

So at 19, the pension qualifies only if it isn't hit by the 10% federal tax (for example, disability or equal periodic payments) and it is the taxpayer's own benefit. Neither PolicyEngine nor TAXSIM charges the 10% tax on this record: federal tax is essentially the same at ages 19 and 65. That means both treat `pensions` as an ordinary, non-early pension, and under that reading the Maine deduction applies. Did TaxAct treat it as an early distribution (1099-R code 1, with the 10% tax on the federal return)?

TAXSIM on this row (age 19):
- The 08-13 build deducts $0, matching TaxAct: tax $18,101.69.
- The current 09-01 build deducts $35,000.

With the age set to 65, both builds deduct $35,000. The 2024 maximum is $45,864: line P2 of the worksheet prints 45,864.00, and the booklet (p. 2) says the deduction "is increased to the maximum annual benefit" under Social Security.

What convention do you want for `pensions` received under 59½? We could treat it as an early distribution (no Maine deduction, and the 10% federal tax) or as an ordinary pension (deductible, no 10% tax). Federal and Maine should agree either way. Our Maine deduction is `me_pension_income_deduction`. It applies the 59½ test only to retirement-account distributions, not to TAXSIM's `pensions`.
